ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two horizontal straight lines marked with the same arrow symbols, indicating that they are parallel; a slanted line as a transversal intersects the two parallel lines respectively. The upper-left angle at the upper intersection is labeled (6y+10)°. The upper-right angle at the lower intersection is labeled (8x−12)°, and the lower-left angle is labeled 4x°. Reasoning: According to the positions in the figure, (8x−12)° and 4x° are vertical angles at the lower intersection, so they are equal: 8x−12=4x. Solving gives 4x=12, so x=3, and 4x=12°. The upper-left angle at the lower intersection forms a linear pair with 4x°, so this angle is 180°−12°=168°. Since the two horizontal lines are parallel, this lower upper-left angle and the upper labeled (6y+10)° are corresponding angles, so 6y+10=168. Solving gives 6y=158, y=158/6≈26.3.

Finally, use corresponding angles between the parallel lines to equate that lower-left-above angle to the top angle labeled (6y+10)°, then solve 6y+10 = that angle for y, giving approximately 26.3.
